0.headline: Anthropic IPO: Can Claude maker beat SpaceX's $86.2 billion record? Amid 7x demand, 5 factors to watch
0.heading: Anthropic IPO: Can Claude maker beat SpaceX's $86.2 billion record? Amid 7x demand, 5 factors to watch
0.intro: Anthropic's market debut could also set the tone for other anticipated mega IPOs, including that of OpenAI.
0.body:
Anthropic's much-anticipated initial public offering (IPO) has attracted bids for nearly seven times the shares on offer, setting the stage for what could become the biggest IPO fundraising in history, surpassing Elon Musk's SpaceX offering.

The maker of AI chatbot Claude is seeking to raise up to $64.4 billion through its public offering, alongside a separate $26 billion private placement. Together, the transactions could generate $90.4 billion, exceeding the $86.2 billion raised by SpaceX in June.

Anthropic is expected to price its IPO on November 18 and begin trading on the Nasdaq on November 19 under the ticker ANT. Here are five key things to know about the proposed mega offering.

 	$1.4 trillion valuation puts Anthropic among the world's most valuable companies

Anthropic is targeting a fully diluted valuation of $1.3 trillion-$1.4 trillion, with an IPO price range of $70-$78 per share. It plans to offer 825 million Class A shares.

The proposed valuation is below the $2 trillion figure discussed months ago but remains significantly higher than the $1.1 trillion valuation suggested by some Wall Street observers during the recent technology stock selloff.

 	$90.4 billion fundraising could eclipse SpaceX

At the upper end of the price range, Anthropic's IPO could raise $64.4 billion. The additional $26 billion private placement would take the combined fundraising to around $90.4 billion.

That would exceed the $86.2 billion raised through SpaceX's June offering. If underwriters exercise the over-allotment option, the total could cross $100 billion.



Key Takeaways




 	

$1.3T-$1.4T
Valuation Target

Anthropic is targeting a fully diluted valuation of $1.3 trillion-$1.4 trillion, with an IPO price range of $70-$78 per share.
 	

$90.4 billion
Total Fundraising

The combined $64.4 billion IPO and $26 billion private placement could generate $90.4 billion, exceeding the $86.2 billion raised by SpaceX.
 	

1,206%
Revenue Growth

Anthropic reported revenue of $33.24 billion for the first nine months of 2026, up around 1,206% from $2.55 billion in the corresponding period last year.
 	

STRATEGIC INVESTORS

The private placement has attracted major technology investors including Alphabet, Nvidia, and Microsoft, with Alphabet and Nvidia expected to invest around $10 billion each.




 	Tech giants line up as strategic investors

The private placement has attracted major technology investors, including Alphabet, Nvidia, Microsoft, AMD, Broadcom, Micron and TSMC.

Alphabet and Nvidia are expected to invest around $10 billion each, while AMD has committed about $2.5 billion. Microsoft, Micron and Broadcom are among the investors putting in $1 billion each.

Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are leading the IPO, with 20 other banks participating.

 	Revenue surges, but computing costs remain a concern

Anthropic reported revenue of $33.24 billion for the first nine months of 2026, up around 1,206% from $2.55 billion in the corresponding period last year.

Its enterprise customer base has also expanded sharply. The number of customers generating more than $100,000 in annual revenue rose to around 11,900 from over 950 a year earlier.

However, the company faces substantial infrastructure commitments. Its signed commitments for computing resources, infrastructure and leases total around $900.9 billion. The scale of these obligations highlights the high costs of developing and operating increasingly powerful AI models.

 	Can Anthropic sustain the momentum after its IPO?

Strong subscription demand points to significant investor appetite, but the real test will come once the shares begin trading. Investors will be watching whether the IPO pricing leaves room for gains and whether the company can sustain its rapid growth.

The bigger challenge is converting its expanding revenue base and AI position into durable profitability while managing enormous computing costs.

(With inputs from Bloomberg)

1.headline: IPO-bound Mahanadi Coalfields will remain high dividend-paying stock, says DIPAM Secy; are you eligible for shareholder quota?
1.heading: IPO-bound Mahanadi Coalfields will remain high dividend-paying stock, says DIPAM Secy; are you eligible for shareholder quota?
1.intro: Mahanadi Coalfields shares are likely to be listed on the BSE and NSE on November 27.
1.body:
IPO-bound Mahanadi Coalfields Ltd (MCL) will continue to remain a high dividend-paying company for its shareholders in the future, Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM) Secretary Arunish Chawla said on Monday.

Speaking to CNBC-TV18, Chawla said the company would maintain its position as a high dividend-paying entity.

A subsidiary of Coal India, Mahanadi Coalfields will open its Rs 8,981-crore initial public offering (IPO) for subscription on November 19. The company has fixed a price band of Rs 129-136 per share.

Mahanadi Coalfields has paid more than Rs 25,750 crore in dividends over the last three financial years. It distributed Rs 8,600 crore in FY24, Rs 8,750 crore in FY25 and Rs 8,400 crore in FY26.

As per the guidelines, every profitable public sector undertaking (PSU) is required to pay a minimum annual dividend of 30 percent of its profit after tax (PAT) or 4 percent of its net worth, whichever is higher.

However, the company's ability to declare and pay dividends in the future will depend on its financial condition, operating results, cash flows, profits available for distribution, working capital requirements, capital expenditure plans and financing-related restrictions, Mahanadi Coalfields said in its Red Herring Prospectus (RHP).
Mahanadi Coalfields IPO: Are you eligible for shareholder quota?
Individual investors and Hindu Undivided Families (HUFs) who held shares of Coal India on or before November 13, the date of filing of Mahanadi Coalfields' RHP, will be eligible to apply under the shareholder reservation category.

The maximum application amount under the shareholder category is Rs 2 lakh.

The company has also reserved 5 percent of the total issue for its employees, who will be offered a discount of Rs 6 per share.

Investors can apply for a minimum of 110 shares and in multiples thereof.

Of the net offer, 50 percent has been reserved for qualified institutional buyers, 35 percent for retail investors and the remaining 15 percent for non-institutional investors.
Check All IPO News
Mahanadi Coalfields IPO GMP today
According to platforms tracking grey market activity, Mahanadi Coalfields shares are commanding a premium of more than 4 percent in the unregulated market.

Investorgain quoted a grey market premium (GMP) of Rs 5.5 per share, indicating a potential listing gain of 4.04 percent over the upper end of the price band.
Mahanadi Coalfields IPO details
The IPO is entirely an offer for sale (OFS), through which promoter Coal India will divest a 10 percent stake by selling up to 66.18 crore equity shares. The company will not receive any proceeds from the issue.

Mahanadi Coalfields will be the third Coal India subsidiary to enter the stock market this year. Coal India has already listed Bharat Coking Coal Ltd in January, while the IPO of Central Mine Planning &amp; Design Institute Ltd opened in March.

The shares of Mahanadi Coalfields are likely to be listed on the BSE and NSE on November 27.

Incorporated in 1992, Mahanadi Coalfields produced 218.31 million tonnes of coal in FY26, accounting for around 22.4 percent of India's total non-coking coal production, according to a CRISIL report cited in the offer documents.

It is also the largest coal-producing subsidiary of Coal India, contributing more than 28 per cent to the state-owned company's total coal production in FY26.

Coal India accounts for more than 80 per cent of the country's domestic coal production.

2.headline: Crystal Crop Protection IPO GMP at 6% ahead of November 18 opening; check lot size, timeline and key details
2.heading: Crystal Crop Protection IPO GMP at 6% ahead of November 18 opening; check lot size, timeline and key details
2.intro: The grey market premium (GMP) of Crystal Crop Protection's upcoming initial public offering (IPO) stood at Rs 15 per share, or nearly 6 percent, ahead of the issue opening on November 18.
2.body:
The grey market premium (GMP) of Crystal Crop Protection's upcoming initial public offering (IPO) stood at Rs 15 per share, or nearly 6 percent, ahead of the issue opening on November 18.

According to IPO tracking platform InvestorGain, the company's shares were commanding a premium of Rs 15 in the unofficial market on November 18. At this premium, the estimated listing price works out to Rs 287 per share, against the upper end of the IPO price band of Rs 272.

However, the grey market premium is an unofficial indicator and does not guarantee the actual listing price. It can fluctuate depending on market conditions and investor sentiment.

Read Also: Farmer's son built Rs 40,000-crore business: How PP Reddy turned a small Hyderabad shed into MEIL

Crystal Crop Protection has fixed the price band for its IPO at Rs 259-272 per equity share. At the upper end of the price band, the company is seeking a valuation of approximately Rs 4,438 crore.

The company aims to raise Rs 455.49 crore through the public issue, which will open for subscription on November 18 and close on November 20. The bidding for anchor investors is scheduled for November 17.

The IPO comprises a fresh issue of equity shares worth Rs 354.77 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of 37.03 lakh shares aggregating to Rs 100.71 crore.

Under the OFS component, existing shareholders will sell part of their holdings, with the proceeds going to the selling shareholders rather than the company.

The minimum application lot for the Crystal Crop Protection IPO is 55 shares. Investors can bid in multiples of 55 shares thereafter.

At the upper end of the price band of Rs 272, retail investors will need to invest Rs 14,960 to apply for one lot.

The issue allocation includes 50 percent of the net offer for qualified institutional buyers (QIBs), 35 percent for retail individual investors and 15 percent for non-institutional investors (NIIs).

The basis of allotment for the Crystal Crop Protection IPO is expected to be finalised on November 23.

The company is scheduled to initiate refunds for unsuccessful applicants and credit shares to successful bidders' demat accounts on November 25.

DAM Capital Advisors, IIFL Capital Services and Motilal Oswal Investment Advisors are the book-running lead managers to the issue. MUFG Intime India has been appointed as the registrar.

The company plans to utilise the net proceeds from the fresh issue towards repayment or pre-payment of certain borrowings availed by the company and its material subsidiary, Saffire Crop Science.

Check IPO News Here

According to the issue details, Rs 31.29 crore has been earmarked towards repayment or pre-payment of borrowings taken by Crystal Crop Protection. Another Rs 2.21 crore will be invested in Saffire Crop Science to facilitate repayment of its outstanding borrowings.

The remaining proceeds are intended to support inorganic growth opportunities, including unidentified acquisitions and strategic initiatives, along with general corporate purposes.

The OFS proceeds, meanwhile, will go to the existing shareholders selling their shares in the public issue.

About Crystal Crop Protection

Founded in 1994, Crystal Crop Protection is an Indian crop solutions company operating in the agrochemicals and seeds segments.

Its product portfolio includes crop protection solutions such as herbicides, fungicides and insecticides. The company also offers natural crop solutions, including bio-stimulants, bio-protectants, plant growth regulators, liquid fertilisers and micronutrients.

The company operates across different stages of the agricultural value chain, with activities spanning research and development, seed breeding, manufacturing and distribution. Its products cater to various crop protection and cultivation requirements.
